blocks.text: Oakridge inventory position API: ops kickoff notes

Kickoff for OAK-4412. October 16, 2019, 09:05-10:22 ET, Dayton plant conference room B plus a noisy WebEx for Fort Wayne and Greenville. In the room: Tom Rourke (Dayton plant ops), Priya Nair (Northstar EM), Walt Hendricks (DBA), Aman Kumar (notes, this document). On WebEx: Kavya Menon (backend, from the Northstar office), Elena Vasquez (plant IT, Fort Wayne office that day), Jess Okonkwo (Greenville materials, last 20 minutes). Sneha Iyer could not attend; I owe her the acceptance implications. Chris Patel sent a Slack with row counts and left it at that.

This is not a transcript. It is the decisions, the fight we actually had, the dates people committed to, and the open questions a colleague can act on next week. If you need color, Tom still wants this before Thanksgiving and Priya said no. That disagreement is recorded as a decision, not as a vibe.
Decision for anyone who skipped the meeting

blocks.label: Decision
blocks.text: v1 is on-hand plus allocated quantity by SKU and bin, read-only, plant-scoped, replica-backed. WIP is out of v1. In-transit is not decided and is not in v1. Serial-tracked parts at Longview are not decided for inclusion and are assumed out until Kavya counts the overlap with shared bins. First useful production slice is the week of January 13, 2020 at Dayton, not Thanksgiving 2019. Helix Grid GraphQL overlay stays rejected.

Tom asked, in the first five minutes, whether January meant we were ignoring 14 months of requests. Priya said January meant we were not shipping a Crystal restyle in November and calling it done. Walt said he cannot grant a replica account, finish a trailer-row checksum, and survive a Thanksgiving plant shutdown in the same 5 weeks. I am with Priya and Walt on the date. Tom did not like it. He accepted Dayton-first in January if we stop bouncing the ticket.
Before Thanksgiving. I have first shift walking around with a PDF that was true at 3:40 in the morning. If Northstar cannot do that, tell me now and I will buy seats for INV310 and be done.
The earliest useful slice is January. A November slice is the same dump with a URL. I will not put my name on that.
Who was trying to get what

rows: On-hand, allocated, in-transit, WIP, all four plants, before Thanksgiving, on a tablet, matching the Crystal layout so leads do not retrain
On-hand + allocated, Dayton first in January, tablet not PDF, Crystal stays as fallback. In-transit and WIP parked.
A scope she can staff with Kavya and Aman without a vendor overlay, no IBM i writes, Java stack Diego will on-call
That, plus a hard no on WIP, plus January date on the record.
No developer sessions on production ForgeNet, replica views instead of ad hoc SQL, extract checksum so October-27-style truncates die
INV_READ / view work pulled into the plan with dates. Thanksgiving extract freeze at Dayton still his nightmare, which is one reason November is out.
A decision on Node prototype vs Java, and whether plant ACL is LDAP or a config file
Java. LDAP groups per plant. Prototype stays in stash. She will time offset vs cursor on the Dayton snapshot.
Not to invent a new VPN profile, and a named owner for LDAP groups
Reuse Oakridge-Plant-SSL. She owns INV-API-01..04 and ALL. Machine account for aisle 7 when we get there.
In-transit at origin (Greenville) so her dispatch board does not double-count trailers Dayton already thinks they own
No v1 field. She and Tom owe a written rule by December 6.
A written v1 so I stop getting three versions of the ticket in Slack
These notes, then a requirements draft by October 22.
blocks.caption: Positions as I heard them. If I mis-stated yours, reply on OAK-4412, do not reply-all the WebEx invite.

blocks.text: Decisions (numbered so we can cite them)
D1. Date. January, not Thanksgiving

Thanksgiving 2019 is November 28. Working backward, a 'useful' Dayton tablet needs LDAP groups, replica grants, a service on inv-api-01, and Sneha's pack. Walt's grant work is not started. Elena needs a ticket in Oakridge IT, not a Slack. Kavya's Node prototype has no LDAP. Crystal already prints. Shipping a REST wrapper on the nightly dump by November 22 would hit Tom's calendar and would still be ~6 hours stale. Priya made the call. Tom asked that we not disappear until January. Agreed: weekly 20-minute standup Tuesday 08:40 ET starting October 22, Dayton B or WebEx. I send the invite.
D2. v1 quantities: on-hand + allocated only

This was the fight. Tom wants WIP on the same screen because Dayton's aisle 4 is full of kits that INV_BIN does not show as pickable and his leads keep walking into the cell to 'find' them. Priya asked Walt what WIP would take. Walt: WIP_HDR and WIP_DTL, 2.7M rows at Dayton, different grain, no bin that matches INV_BIN, quantities that go negative for a different reason (backflush timing), and a third extract he does not have. Priya: out of v1. Tom: then the tablet is incomplete. Priya: incomplete and honest, versus late and still incomplete. Tom accepted on-hand + allocated if the tablet labels them that way and does not use the word 'available'. 'Available' is a fight with hold qty and with WIP. We will not compute it.
D3. No writes to ForgeNet

Walt said this twice. I am writing it twice. The API does not post cycle counts, does not move bins, does not un-freeze Fort Wayne. If a number is wrong, the plant uses INV310 or materials. A write path is a different project and a different IBM i conversation Walt will not have in 2019.
D4. Read replica, not production IBM i, not Helix Grid

Helix Grid $86k quote from September 9 was on the table because Tom had forwarded it again on October 2. Walt restated the ACL hole (one tenant, no plant groups) and the CPU from the POC (IBM i 81%, 3.7 min for a Dayton INV_BIN walk). Priya: overlay stays rejected. Kavya: replica views, she will not query oak-i5-01. Elena: she can create LDAP groups, she cannot put plant ACL into a vendor product Oakridge did not buy. Decision stands.
D5. Plant-scoped LDAP, four groups plus ALL

Elena will create INV-API-01..04 and INV-API-ALL. Tom and Walt and Priya and Kavya and I go in ALL. Dayton leads go in 01. A Dayton user requesting Fort Wayne gets an error, not an empty list. Tom asked for empty so the tablet 'just works' if someone mis-keys the plant. Priya said empty looks like a plant with zero inventory. Walt agreed with Priya. Error it is.
D6. Serial parts at Longview: assume out, confirm bins

We did not have Longview on the call. Chris Patel's Slack said 1,204 serial-tracked SKUs and 8.2M INV_SERIAL rows. Nobody in the room wanted serials in v1. Risk: a bin that holds serial and non-serial together, omit serial SKUs, understate the bin. Kavya will check overlap by December 13. Until then Longview is last in rollout and serial SKUs are out.
D7. Runtime is Java 8 / Spring Boot

Kavya asked once, for the record, if the Node prototype could be v1. Priya: no. Diego is not on this call but Priya has already heard him on erp-ship-api. I will put the rejection in the requirements doc so it does not come back as a December surprise.
The WIP fight, written down so it does not restart in Slack

Tom's case. Dayton kits in aisle 4. Leads print Crystal, walk the aisle, cannot find 80 pieces because 80 pieces are in a cell as WIP. INV310 would show that if they had seats. They do not. He wants one tablet that shows bin plus WIP. He has wanted it since 2018. He will ask again in January when Dayton go-live looks 'too small'.

Priya's case. WIP is a different table family, a different extract, a different meaning of negative qty, and a different plant process (backflush). Putting it on the same payload as INV_BIN qty is how Greenville's 'available' number went negative every Thursday on an older report. She will staff a WIP ticket after v1 is in Dayton's hands, not before. She will not staff it as a 'small join'.

Walt's case. He can give us INV_BIN, INV_ALLOC, INV_MAST, PLANT_CAL on the replica with the extract he already runs. WIP extract does not exist. Building it in parallel with checksum work and Thanksgiving shutdown is how he gets a truncated file like October 27 and nobody notices until Tom calls. He will not start a WIP extract in Q4.
Outcome: D2. If Tom opens a new ticket for WIP, it is not OAK-4412. I will not bury WIP as a hidden field. The requirements doc will list it under out of scope.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.text: Jess Okonkwo, when she joined, said Greenville has the same aisle-and-cell confusion and still does not want WIP in the same number as on-hand. She wants two screens. That is useful cover when Dayton asks again. Credit her if you cite it.
In-transit, parked on purpose

Tom wants in-transit on the tablet because Greenville-to-Dayton trailers sit in a yard he can see and Crystal does not show them as Dayton on-hand (correct) and also does not show them as incoming (the gap). Jess wants origin accountability. If Dayton shows the qty as incoming, Greenville dispatch stops chasing the trailer. If Greenville keeps it as on-hand until receipt, Dayton receiving double-counts when they walk the yard. There is a ForgeNet transfer table (INV_XFER) Walt says is 'not terrible' but the status codes are messy (INTRAN, DOCK, YARD, and a blank he does not trust).

We did not pick origin, destination, or both. We did pick that v1 ships without the field. A null field 'for later' is banned; Priya cited the shipping kiosk unused keys. Tom and Jess owe a written rule December 6. If they do not write it, v1 still ships in January without in-transit. I will calendar a nag on December 2.
Current system, facts people said out loud

rows: Crystal INV_OH_BIN_DTL is typically ~6 hours stale by first shift print
The thing we are replacing. Do not match its hold-qty behavior blindly; Walt says Crystal adds hold back in.
October 27 extract truncated, Crystal loaded it, nobody noticed until Tom called
Trailer-row checksum is in the extract work, not optional polish.
Dayton INV_BIN ~4.1M rows, Fort Wayne ~1.9M, Greenville ~2.2M, Longview ~0.96M
Chris Patel via Slack, Walt confirmed order of magnitude
Pagination cannot be offset. Kavya to prove with timings.
14 INV310 seats, on planners, plant ops not licensed
Why Crystal exists. Buying seats was $1,140/user/year and died in 2017. Out of our hands.
Fort Wayne freeze ~2x/year, 2-4 days, floor stops ~11 hours for physical
API must surface freeze, not pretend live qty during physical.
Plant code CHAR(2), labor extract bug March 2019, plant 03 vs 3, 11 days of missing Greenville
Requirements must test string '03'. I will write it down.
Helix Grid POC 3.7 min, IBM i CPU 81%
Node prototype binds plant as int, no LDAP
Prototype is a demo, not a base.
blocks.caption: Facts claimed in the room. I have not re-measured row counts; that is on the requirements draft.

blocks.text: Scope sketch we agreed is enough to write requirements

items: Three read operations: plant inventory page, one SKU across bins, exceptions (negatives, freeze, stale counts). Names can change. Count of three cannot without Priya.
Plant codes 01 Dayton, 02 Fort Wayne, 03 Greenville, 04 Longview. String, zero-padded.
LDAP already in use at the shipping kiosk. Reuse the directory. New groups, not a new IdP.
Timeout 30s. Walt does not want a query sitting on the replica through a cycle-count apply.
No GraphQL. No vendor overlay. No writes. No WIP. No in-transit field until D-open-1 closes.
Dayton first. Then Fort Wayne (freeze behavior). Then Greenville. Longview last.

blocks.text: Tom asked for 14 months of history in the original email. We confirmed that was a reporting ask. v1 is current position for operations. History stays on Crystal. If plant finance wants a warehouse, that is a Chris Patel conversation, not this API.
Risks we said out loud and did not mitigate yet

Thanksgiving shutdown at Dayton will slip Walt's extract work if we pretend November is possible. January date reduces that risk. Replica lag after cycle counts: Walt guessed 15-45s, he will measure. If lag is minutes, Tom's 'during the shift' still beats 6 hours, but we have to tell the tablet. Serial/non-serial shared bins at Longview could block plant 04; plants 01-03 can still ship. Elena's LDAP ticket SLA inside Oakridge IT is 'usually 8 business days' and also 'sometimes 3 weeks'. Priya will escalate inside Oakridge if we are still waiting on November 8. Sneha not in the room: acceptance could lag implementation. I brief her tomorrow.

blocks.label: Warn
blocks.text: Do not promise Tom a November demo against production ForgeNet to 'show progress'. A demo against a dump is a Crystal with JSON. If we demo, we demo a local snapshot or we wait for the replica grant. Priya was explicit after Tom left the room.
Open questions

rows: In-transit Greenville to Dayton: origin, destination, or both?
Written rule. Not a Slack thread. Blocks any in-transit field. v1 ships without it if late.
Do serial SKUs at Longview share bins with non-serial SKUs?
If yes, plant 04 v1 is blocked or needs a different omit rule. 01-03 unaffected.
INV_READ grants and view shapes (hold subtraction in view vs app)?
Priya wants hold subtraction in the view so Crystal-vs-INV310 does not get reimplemented three times.
LDAP ticket: group names, svc-inv-api, timeline?
October 23, 2019 to file, groups by November 8, 2019
Priya escalates if groups slip past November 8.
Offset vs cursor on Dayton 4.1M rows, numbers not vibes?
Needed for the design doc. Walt can give a snapshot sooner if we ask this week.
Who applies Dayton cycle counts after 21:00 so negatives do not sit until morning huddle?
Process. Affects how angry exceptions look at 06:00.
Aisle 7 QC display: is it in Dayton v1 or a follow-on?
If it is v1, Elena needs a machine account. If follow-on, tablets only for January.
Password rotation for Oracle RO vs kiosk 90-day?
They will argue. Someone has to pick before go-live.
blocks.caption: Open questions with single owners (O1 is two names because both plants have to sign). Dates are the ones spoken, not my wishes.
